title.narrative: Informing actions to protect tropical forests through journalism

description.narrative: Journalism on tropical forests in Brazil and other Latinamerican countries. Efforts to reduce market pressure for commodities associated with tropical deforestation and improve sustainable forest land use will progress faster and more efficiently by mobilizing a global network of journalists capable of improving transparency about critical and underreported social and environmental challenges and solutions. Decision-makers, at all levels, as well as the general public, urgently need trusted, clear, timely, and actionable information to appreciate the risks associated with tropical forest loss adequately and to inform actions that address vulnerabilities related to climate and environmental change, while building resilience to these risks. This project improves awareness of the drivers of tropical deforestation through consistent multi-lingual publication, identifying opportunities for effective forest conservation and sustainable livelihoods, and amplifying the voices of Indigenous peoples and low-income communities. Through this project, Mongabay will engage a consortium of local, regional, and global partners capable of sourcing information in tropical forest countries via community networks and earth observation data; exposing hidden drivers of deforestation through investigative reporting of commodity supply chains, beneficial ownership, and nature crime; providing professional opportunities for journalists in tropical forest countries to improve their skills and earn a decent living; and inform a large global audience needed to create an enabling environment for the sustainable development of tropical forests across the world.
